page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the N2 family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.8 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and includes 33 MB of L3 cache. This configuration does not bundle local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results place the n2-standard-8 in the average tier for most multi-core CPU operations, memory bandwidth, and database workloads. Specifically, the instance achieves average performance in Passmark CPU tests, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput. However, single-core CPU performance and multi-threaded decompression tasks fall into the lower 25th percentile. Memory bandwidth remains stable at 50.27 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 37.18 GB/sec for uncached writes.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the n2-standard-8 offers a standard resource density suitable for general-purpose workloads. It is well-suited for web serving, software compilation, database operations, and moderate text processing. The lack of local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators makes it less optimal for high-performance storage-heavy databases or intensive machine learning training, though it can handle basic low-parameter LLM text generation at average speeds.
